text:
Some teams win on hot goaltending and some on hot shooting. Vegas is winning on neither. The Golden Knights are 11-5-2 with 59 goals for on 59.8 expected and 49 against on 49.2 expected, and their 24 points sit within two of what their chances deserved. Our simulations give them a 95% playoff chance and a 43% share of the Pacific. It is a sturdy, sustainable start.

The penalty kill is the edge. Vegas allows 0.48 expected goals a game shorthanded, and Jesse Granger of The Athletic called it "a difference maker." Mark Stone, Ivan Barbashev and Jack Eichel have played 166 minutes together and outscored teams 9-4. Brayden McNabb and Shea Theodore have logged 266 minutes as a pair, winning 61% of the chances, plus-8 in goals.

There are soft spots. The second pair of Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon has 36% of the expected goals, and the Nic Dowd line is at 31% and has been outscored 5-1. Mitch Marner's line with William Karlsson and Brett Howden has been a step behind the top unit.

Victor Olofsson has six points in five games against 2.7 expected. Fun, and temporary. The interesting question for Vegas is the playoff one: whether that second pair can be trusted in April.
headline: Vegas is exactly as good as it looks
